findings.summary: `reporter_tier` exists only in the generated TypeScript mirror; no migration in the reviewed range or repository adds the column to `agents`.
findings.scenario: Deploying onto a database built from repository migrations causes Feed, ingest, extraction, editing, and posting queries that select or update `reporter_tier` to fail with a missing-column error.

findings.summary: A standard inference fills a null desk tier without preserving an existing premium tier for the same linked reporter, so the new desk value masks stronger premium evidence.
findings.scenario: A reporter's linked `x_accounts` row is already proven premium, but a new 50-post extraction sample contains no long post; extraction writes `reporter_tier = "standard"`, and all four resolved gates incorrectly fall from 25,000 to 280 characters.

findings.summary: Website publisher-mention normalization runs after the primary model call is persisted, so changing `written.call.output` cannot alter the durable draft read by Feed or posting.
findings.scenario: The model emits `@publisher.example`; Slack receives the normalized in-memory text, but the winner references the already-persisted unnormalized output, so the reporter sees and can publish the erroneous mention.

findings.summary: `editDraft` discards errors from its `reporter_tier` query and silently falls back to the posting-account tier, breaking the required agreement between edit and post gates.
findings.scenario: For a premium-reporter desk using a standard posting account, a transient agents-query error makes a 500-character edit fail at 280, while `post-core` later reads the premium desk tier and accepts the same text.

findings.summary: The English fast path trusts the language hint even though the revised translation contract declares it unreliable and requires inspection of every meaningful non-English segment.
findings.scenario: An article marked `en` contains a Spanish headline or quotation; translation is skipped and the untranslated text is passed to the drafter as the supposedly canonical English source.

findings.summary: The server action does not enforce the new 30-character agent-name limit, leaving the cap dependent on the client form.
findings.scenario: A crafted or stale Server Action request submits a name longer than 30 characters; `createDesk` checks only that it is nonempty and persists a name that violates the workspace and switcher contract.

findings.summary: Mobile publication names cannot shrink, truncate, or wrap, allowing the new model-authored labels to push the timestamp and Draft menu outside the clipped card.
findings.scenario: A 60-character publication name is rendered on a narrow phone; the fixed label, timestamp, and controls exceed the strip width, making freshness information and the menu partially or completely inaccessible.

findings.summary: Favicons are fetched directly from monitored publishers in the reporter's browser, creating a passive third-party tracking channel.
findings.scenario: Opening Feed or Sources requests `/favicon.ico` from each visible publisher, disclosing the reporter's IP, user agent, Oparax referrer origin, and viewing time to those third parties.
